title: Hampton's endless rehearsals and the cattle-car trip to Oakland
summary: Hampton called rehearsals out of loneliness; after a night on a cattle car the band reached Oakland at four and was told to rehearse at six.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Right. Right. And love what he done. Only one bad feature about him that I disliked, he wants his musicians (inaudible) what you call rehearsals. He might rehearse another (inaudible) and end up playing the first one. But he keep you there all day.

And I said this. The man was lonely. He didn't have the right thing with him -- you know, his marriage -- so he needed a band with him, somebody where he could play his instrument (inaudible) that he had the control over and (inaudible) so he called rehearsal.
We left Kansas City on a cattle car and (inaudible) going to Oakland. Hamp and Gladys catches the Chief and go out.
Cattle car, when I say (inaudible) seats, sitting up. No -- sleep the best way you can.

We get in to Oakland and pull in, and Hamp's at the station. (Inaudible) rehearsal at 6:00 o'clock. Yes, he did. Yes, he did. Don't care nothing about you. He's rested. He went in on the fast route. Now he want his band to be at the auditorium in Oakland to rehearse at 6:00, and we ain't even got our rooms yet. And we're getting in at 4:00 o'clock in the evening.
Not a bite to eat, eating sandwiches on the train.
Well, don't the guys tell him something?
